NH-2026-HB1800.title: relative to statewide education property taxes.

actions.text: Interim Study Report: Not Recommended for Future Legislation 10/07/2026 (Vote 13-1;)
Full Committee Work Session: 09/30/2026 10:00 am GP 234
Refer for Interim Study: MA VV 03/05/2026 HJ 6 P. 41

Full Committee Work Session: 02/18/2026 10:00 am GP 154
Full Committee Work Session: 02/09/2026 10:00 am GP 159
Introduced 01/07/2026 and referred to Ways and Means HJ 1 P. 36

NH-2026-HB1800.aiSummary: The bill would change New Hampshire’s statewide education property tax and set it at $5 per $1,000 of property value starting July 1, 2027. It would also create tax credits for a primary home, for people without children in local public schools, and for people over 65. The money would be sent through the state revenue office and then distributed back to municipalities for local school districts, and it would change how the state figures the cost of education grants.

NH-2026-HB1404.title: establishing a study committee to study the equitable division of property in divorce proceedings.

actions.text: Interim Study Report: Not Recommended for Future Legislation 10/21/2026 (Vote 7-1;)

Committee Report: Refer for Interim Study 03/02/2026 (Vote 14-0; CC) HC 10 P. 4
Introduced 01/07/2026 and referred to Children and Family Law HJ 1 P. 19

NH-2026-HB1404.aiSummary: The bill would create a study committee to review how property is divided in divorce cases and to look at laws in New Hampshire and other states. The committee could also suggest new laws if it finds problems, and its members would get mileage pay at the legislative rate when they attend meetings. The act would take effect when passed, and the committee would report its findings and any law ideas by November 1, 2026.

NH-2026-HB1198.title: establishing the paint product stewardship program.

actions.text: Interim Study Report: Recommended for Future Legislation 10/15/2026 (Vote 10-1; )

Committee Report: Refer for Interim Study 02/04/2026 (Vote 16-0; CC) HC 7 P. 4
Introduced 01/07/2026 and referred to Commerce and Consumer Affairs HJ 1 P. 10

NH-2026-HB1198.aiSummary: The bill would create a paint product stewardship program in New Hampshire. Manufacturers of paint sold at retail, or a group that represents them, would have to submit a plan for collecting and handling leftover paint, and retailers and other collection sites could take part if they agree to the plan. The plan would include a per-container fee on paint sold in the state, and manufacturers would also have to file yearly reports and help pay the state’s program costs.

NH-2026-HB1154.title: restricting the texting of unsolicited advertisements, including political campaigns.

actions.text: Interim Study Report: Not Recommended for Future Legislation 10/15/2026 (Vote 11-0; )

Committee Report: Refer for Interim Study 02/04/2026 (Vote 16-0; CC) HC 7 P. 4
Introduced 01/07/2026 and referred to Commerce and Consumer Affairs HJ 1 P. 8

NH-2026-HB1154.aiSummary: The bill would make it unlawful to send unsolicited text ads, including messages for political campaigns, unless the sender has permission or meets certain relationship-based exceptions. It would also require an opt-out notice in those messages and would bar using multiple numbers to get around blocking or opt-out requests. People who break the rule could face criminal charges, civil fines, or a lawsuit, and the act would take effect July 1, 2027.

Introduced 01/07/2026 and referred to Labor, Industrial and Rehabilitative Services HJ 1 P. 35

NH-2026-HB1767.aiSummary: The bill would set unemployment benefits at up to 20 weeks in a year. If statewide weekly claims stay above 4,000 for 3 straight weeks, the limit would rise to 26 weeks, and it would drop back to 20 weeks if claims fall to 4,000 or less for 3 straight weeks. The Department of Employment Security would have to track the claims and update the public and its systems when the limit changes. It would take effect 60 days after passage.
